policy: Erratum: a defect in a pinned source (typo, wrong constant/sign, missing hypothesis, false as stated, gap). A gap counts as an erratum only when a printed assertion is false; a supplied argument for a true step is a deviation. Deviation: a deliberate difference of the formalization from the source (scope, conventions, reformulation, explicit parameter windows, proof supplements, different proof routes). Our own statement repairs are neither.

entries.claim: Proof route: the tori are obtained from an a-posteriori fixed-frequency KAM theorem (parameterization method, no canonical changes of variables) applied at each Diophantine frequency, not by Pöschel's iteration of symplectic transformations

entries.claim: Estimates are carried out in weighted ℓ¹ Fourier(–Taylor) coefficient norms instead of sup norms on complex strips; hypotheses are stated for real-analytic functions and converted once at the interface
entries.effect: constants differ from the printed ones; the frozen statements carry their own explicit constants or are qualitative

entries.claim: Phase space Tⁿ × B is represented in coordinates: angles in ℝⁿ with ℤⁿ-periodicity, actions in an open set of ℝⁿ (no manifold structure, no general symplectic form)
entries.effect: the general exact-symplectic setting of the source is specialized to the standard form on Tⁿ × ℝⁿ
